answer.generated: Referential integrity constraints differ from simple constraint violations because they allow the user to specify alternative actions when a conflict occurs during an update. Unlike other constraints where the system simply rejects the update and signals an error, referential integrity constraints permit the user to choose from predefined options such as cascading updates, setting null values, or ignoring the violation. This flexibility enables more robust database management, as it lets users handle dependencies between tables in a way that maintains consistency without always rolling back changes.
